Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Mature framework with active enforcement and regional alignment
Comments: Data Protection Act 2017 enacted, DPA Commissioner with enforcement powers [DLA Piper](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law&c=MU)
revision_notes: Cited source (DLA Piper) fetched and verified: confirms Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017 (in force since 15 January 2018), modelled on the GDPR. Cross-checked against DLA Piper's enforcement page and the Data Protection Office's 2024 Annual Report, both confirming active enforcement powers (investigation of complaints, enforcement notices, prosecution, right of appeal to the ICT Appeal Tribunal) and annual public reporting to the National Assembly. The UN Special Rapporteur on Privacy, following a 2023 country visit, assessed Mauritius as a regional leader in data privacy, supporting the 'regional alignment' element of the score, though the same report and the DPO's own 2024 Annual Report flag ongoing implementation gaps (a national-security exemption under s.44, and resourcing constraints affecting prosecutions). On balance the evidence supports the existing score. Confirmed unchanged at Value Code 5. Flagged for human review because this is a maximum (top-of-scale) code, per verification policy.
revised_comments: Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017, in force since 15 January 2018, establishes a Data Protection Office headed by a Commissioner with statutory powers to investigate complaints, issue enforcement notices, and pursue prosecutions, with a right of appeal to the ICT Appeal Tribunal. The Office publishes annual reports to the National Assembly and has been assessed by the UN Special Rapporteur on Privacy as a regional leader in data protection, reflecting broad alignment with international standards such as the GDPR and the AU Malabo Convention, notwithstanding some acknowledged implementation and resourcing gaps.
